sanitized_fixture: DEC-003 row 6.16 (Git worktree isolation) exercise: a genuinely-live untagged hcom session (`hale`) was bound via `maps run bind-session` to a run manifest created by `maps flow start --require-worktree-binding --base-revision <HEAD>`, which froze a concrete Git worktree identity (repo_root/git_common_dir/git_dir/worktree_private_dir) into `run_manifest.worktree`. The session process was SIGTERM-killed while the task claim was ACTIVE and its lease still live. recovery-tick pass 1 observed alive (baseline); pass 2 observed the live->not-live transition and opened silent_stop incident RNS-712cbdd544aa with a resolved run_id and resume_after = +900s. After resume_after, `recovery-tick --enforce-canonical-run --harness-project-id maps-lean --repo-root <PATH>` was run with PATH set to (a) a linked `git worktree add` checkout of the same repo at the same HEAD, and (b) a non-git directory. Both produced action `resume_denied` with `harness_resume: {attempted: true, code: "HOOK_DENIED"}`; the incident parked in state `denied` (canonical_denials incremented, transient retry ladder untouched). A direct reproduction of `CanonicalRunGuard.__call__` against the identical TaskStore + run manifest + execution binding (operation="resume") pinned the guard_code: repo_root = linked worktree -> RUN_WORKTREE_MISMATCH ("Run is bound to a different Git worktree than the one continuing it."); repo_root = non-git dir -> RUN_WORKTREE_UNAVAILABLE ("Current Git worktree identity could not be read for a worktree-bound run."); repo_root = the original bound clone -> `_require_bound_worktree` returns None (worktree seam passes; any denial there is a downstream session-lineage check, not the worktree seam). First real production-path exposure of `_require_bound_worktree` / RUN_WORKTREE_MISMATCH / RUN_WORKTREE_UNAVAILABLE.
